text:
lara: Heads up — CI flagged a perf regression on PR #6237 after merge. Microbench `kv_batcher::process_batch` p99 jumped ~35% and CPU heatmaps show kernel routing changes around the same time.

ci-bot: Perf check failed for PR 6237 (branch: feature/batch-routing). CI run: https://ci.redwood/example/6237 — failing test: `perf/micro/kv_batch_p99` threshold +0.35 (expected <=0.10).

ashwin: ugh. I saw increased serialization in the batching path on my local smoke runs yesterday. Possibly the new bucketizer change we merged yesterday.

mike: can we bisect quickly? suspecting commit range: `a1f3..b2d8` (kernel selector refactor + bucketizer tweak). I can start a bisect job unless someone already has one.

olivia: I ran a short bisect on a staging subset — rough notes: revert of `b2c1` (bucketizer:prefer-closer-lengths) brought p99 back to baseline. Patch `b2c1` introduces an extra pass that changes batching groups (and thus kernel selection).

lara: thanks olivia. do we have a repro script for the microbench so CI can run targeted bisect?

mike: yes, script is `bench/kv_batcher_repro.sh` — runs with same seed and request mix as CI. Example run: 
```
./bench/kv_batcher_repro.sh --model redwood-small --iters 2000 --concurrency 64
```
Outputs p99 numbers and per-kernel invocation counts.

ashwin: FYI adding the extra bucket pass was an attempt to reduce cross-sequence padding but it groups short and long sequences differently which can flip kernel selection heuristics (fp16 vs int8 fast path). That explains the higher p99 on our long-tail scenario.

ci-bot: Bisect job started by mike @ 1769585002. Link: https://ci.redwood/bisect/987

mike: bisect results (summary): 
- good: a1f3 (baseline)
- bad: b2d8 (current)
- culprit: b2c1 (bucketizer: prefer-closer-lengths)

olivia: flamegraph snippets from before/after: 
```
before: kernel_fp16_avg  72%  kernel_int8_avg  18%  other 10%
after:  kernel_fp16_avg  48%  kernel_int8_avg  40%  other 12%
```
shows more int8 kernel usage post-change (slower for these sequence-length mixes).

ashwin: hmm interesting — int8 codegen is slower for the long-seq kv loops on Ampere due to extra dequant rounds. My bad, I missed that in perf matrix.

lara: two options: 1) revert b2c1 immediately to unblock rollout, or 2) tweak bucketizer to enforce sequence-length homogeneity threshold so kernel selector keeps fp16 fast path for long-tail traffic. Thoughts?

ben: revert is safest short-term. We should also add a targeted microbench in CI that asserts per-kernel proportions don't change >10% across PRs for the long-tail fixture.

mike: agree on revert + guard. I'll open a revert PR now and add a perf test. Patch name: `revert-b2c1-kv-bucketizer`

olivia: also adding a perf note in the PR explaining why bucketizer changes affect kernel routing (so model owners know the coupling).

ci-bot: Revert PR opened by mike: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6254 at 1769585720

lara: great. once CI passes with revert we'll rollout. Also schedule follow-up to design the threshold-based bucketizer with test coverage.

ashwin: I'll own the follow-up. Plan: run matrix across hardware (V100/A100/Ampere) + quant types to find safe heuristics.

mike: local CI with revert shows microbench p99 back to baseline: before 28.2ms -> after revert 20.9ms (baseline 21.1ms).

ci-bot: CI passed for revert PR #6254 at 1769586100.

lara: thanks all — leaving an action item: add a perf regression guard (kernel-proportion check) + update docs for bucketizer-kernel coupling. :white_check_mark:

ben: noted. I'll add the CI test template and a short blurb to the perf playbook.

lara: closing the thread once the revert is merged to main.
